memory_note: UNIFIED. CPU and GPU share physical RAM - no PCIe, no host-device copies.

toolchain.note: COMMAND LINE TOOLS ONLY - full Xcode is NOT installed.
toolchain.xcrun_metal: ABSENT - there is no offline .metal -> .air -> .metallib compiler
toolchain.consequence: Shaders MUST be compiled at RUNTIME via newLibraryWithSource:options:error:. Metal.framework does this itself and needs no Xcode.
toolchain.build_example: clang++ -O2 -std=c++17 -x objective-c++ -fobjc-arc main.mm -o app -framework Foundation -framework Metal

notes: METAL SHADING LANGUAGE HAS NO double TYPE. Verified on this machine: the runtime compiler REJECTS a kernel declaring 'device double*'. There is no slow FP64 to fall back on - there is none at all.

Reaching 1e-10 therefore requires constructing extended precision from fp32: double-single / double-double (Dekker two-sum, Knuth two-product with fma), compensated summation, or an equivalent error-free transformation.

Double-single gives ~48 mantissa bits against IEEE binary64's 53 - roughly 32x coarser per operation. A CUDA port of this same case measured 2.8e-17 against the reference, so a ~32x coarser port should land near 1e-15, still far inside 1e-10. That is an estimate, not a guarantee.
There is NO cuFFT equivalent. MetalPerformanceShaders does not provide a general 3D double-precision FFT. You must write the transform yourself.
float2 is 8 bytes, exactly like a double, so double-single costs no extra memory traffic - only ALU.
Unified memory means no explicit host-device transfer is required; use MTLResourceStorageModeShared.
